title: VSOCK (VM sockets) packet header
summary: VSOCK provides socket-based communication between a host and a guest VM (or between guests) without a network stack. The packet header: 4-byte src CID, 4-byte dst CID, 4-byte src port, 4-byte dst port, 4-byte type (stream/dgram/seqpacket), 2-byte op, 2-byte flags, 8-byte length, 8-byte socket ID (src/dst).

ext.summary: VSOCK provides socket-based communication between a host and a guest VM (or between guests) without a network stack. The packet header: 4-byte src CID, 4-byte dst CID, 4-byte src port, 4-byte dst port, 4-byte type (stream/dgram/seqpacket), 2-byte op, 2-byte flags, 8-byte length, 8-byte socket ID (src/dst).

structure.meaning: Source context ID (VM ID; 2 = host, 3+ = guest).
Operation: REQUEST, RESPONSE, RST, SHUTDOWN, RW, CREDIT_UPDATE, CREDIT_REQUEST.

ext.example_decoded: VSOCK packet: src CID 2 (host) -> dst CID 3 (guest), ports 4096->8192, stream, RW op
notes: VSOCK uses CID (context ID) to identify VMs; CID 0 = hypervisor, 1 = local (loopback), 2 = host, 3+ = guests.
Well-known ports: 52 (vsock) is not standardized; applications choose ports (e.g. 9p over vsock uses 9p port).
Firecracker exposes vsock as a device with a Unix socket on the host side (vsock.sock).
Credit-based flow control prevents buffer overflow between host and guest.
